concepts.title: Why International Organisations
concepts.definition: International organisations exist because states need forums to cooperate on problems no single state can solve - war prevention, development, health and humanitarian relief - with the UN founded in 1945 after two world wars to save succeeding generations from the scourge of war.
concepts.key_idea: An organisation helps with matters of war and peace and helps countries cooperate to make better living conditions for us all.

solution_steps.explain: collective problems like war need standing institutions
the UN charter took effect in 1945 after the world wars
WHO, UNESCO and UNICEF carry specialised cooperation

concepts.title: Evolution of the UN and Membership
concepts.definition: The UN began in 1945 with 51 founding members and expanded to 193 members as decolonisation admitted new states, changing the General Assembly's majorities and pushing demands to reform the Security Council whose five permanent members hold vetoes.
concepts.key_idea: The growth of UN membership is the current member count minus the founding count of 51.

concepts.title: Reform of the UN
concepts.definition: Reform debates cover two tracks: procedures and relevance - making the Security Council more representative and reworking mandates - with India arguing for permanent membership on grounds of population, democracy, economy and peacekeeping record, while rivals propose alternatives like longer-term seats.
concepts.key_idea: Everyone wants a reformed Council; no one agrees whose seat it should be.
concepts.textbook_ref: leps104.txt reform criteria and India's case sections

solution_steps.explain: one track reworks procedures and priorities, the other the Council's composition
population, democracy, economic size and peacekeeping record are India's planks
regional rivalries and the veto freeze any expansion

concepts.title: India and the UN
concepts.definition: India's UN engagement spans peacekeeping contributions among the largest, leadership of the Non-Aligned and G77, nuclear debate years, and campaigns for Council reform; India uses the UN to project multilateralism while seeking its democratisation.
concepts.key_idea: For India the UN is both stage and stake: it defends multilateral rules while asking for a seat at the top table.
